profile.address: 175, Old Loudon Road, Latham, Town of Colonie, Albany County, New York, 12110
profile.reading:
This building at 175 Old Loudon Road in Latham, in the Town of Colonie just north of Albany, has operated as a purpose-built data center since it was developed under the TurnKey Internet name, a hosting and colocation provider founded in New York's Capital Region. By the time of its 2021 sale, TurnKey Internet served roughly 1,500 customers with dedicated-server, bare-metal, and colocation hosting, and public facility listings put the building's footprint at roughly 25,800 square feet.

On November 9, 2021, Miami-based infrastructure company ColoHouse announced it had acquired TurnKey Internet, describing the deal -- alongside a simultaneous purchase of another provider, Quonix/Data102 -- as ColoHouse's first move into directly owning a data center building rather than leasing space, a notable structural shift for the company. ColoHouse said it intended to keep TurnKey's existing technical staff in place to maintain continuity for customers, use TurnKey's bare-metal expertise to expand that service line across ColoHouse's other markets (which then included Miami, New York, Dallas, and Phoenix), and eventually extend bare-metal hosting into Europe.

ColoHouse's acquisition strategy continued in 2024, when it acquired Hivelocity, a bare-metal and dedicated-server hosting company founded in 2002 that had grown from a single rack of servers in a basement to operations spanning more than 40 data centers across six continents. With both TurnKey Internet and Hivelocity now under common ColoHouse ownership, TurnKey's original retail web domain has since come to redirect visitors to Hivelocity's site, consistent with the two customer-facing brands being consolidated, even though neither company's own marketing materials narrate that consolidation by name. This registry lists the Latham facility's operator as Hivelocity to reflect that current branding, though the property itself is the TurnKey-built building ColoHouse purchased outright in 2021.

Neither ColoHouse nor Hivelocity publishes technical specifications -- power capacity, tier rating, or cooling design -- for the Latham building specifically, which is typical for privately held bare-metal hosting operators that sell service contracts directly to business customers rather than marketing wholesale colocation space to brokers. What is publicly documented is the ownership chain described above, the approximate building size, and the site's long-standing role as a going-concern data center rather than new construction: it has operated continuously as a hosting facility through at least three ownership eras -- independent TurnKey Internet, TurnKey under ColoHouse, and the current Hivelocity-branded operation -- without any reported closure, outage event, or relocation in the public record.

reading.body:
This facility in Latham, New York has no published power specification and therefore cannot be assessed for its capacity to host AI workloads. The operator, Hivelocity, holds SOC2, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, HIPAA, NIST 800-53, GDPR, and CCPA certifications, qualifying it for regulated hosting and compliance-sensitive tenants. The facility itself is not individually named in any operator documentation available to this site.

New York State has 31 mapped data center facilities, of which only one publishes a power figure. This campus ranks second by published megawatts in the state, but that ranking reflects a gap in published data rather than deployed capacity. Without a power specification from the operator, the campus cannot be sized against the state's total or regional AI scaling needs.

The attribution of this facility to Hivelocity is based on domain redirect evidence alone. No fetched source has confirmed the Latham site remains active under the current operator, and the research note flags this for reverification. Any assessment of this campus's role in AI infrastructure must await either a published power specification or explicit confirmation of its current operational status.
